react_result.final_narrative_text: The three-paradigm consensus is unambiguous: tryptophan metabolism is the dominant perturbed pathway, achieving rank 1 in RaMP-ORA (FDR 1.46e-15, fold enrichment 857.8, 6 of 54 pathway metabolites hit), MetaboAnalystR KEGG-ORA (p=1.79e-07, 5 of 41 metabolites hit), and Mummichog m/z-direct analysis (p=0.00479, 14 of 15 network compounds matched). Six tryptophan-derived metabolites drive this signal: the precursor L-tryptophan, the biogenic amine intermediates tryptamine and indoleacetaldehyde, the central neurotransmitter serotonin, the pineal hormone melatonin, and the kynurenine-pathway product quinolinic acid. Two high-confidence sub-pathways are co-enriched: Serotonin and melatonin biosynthesis (REACT:R-HSA-209931, FDR 2.81e-08) and Tryptophan catabolism leading to NAD+ production (WP:WP4210, FDR 7.30e-08), implicating perturbations in both the neurotransmitter and the NAD+-biosynthesis arms of tryptophan catabolism. Succinic acid and D-glucose, while differentially abundant, do not contribute to tryptophan pathway membership and likely reflect downstream metabolic consequences or independent processes. Iron (C14819) is annotated as a cofactor in several tryptophan-converting reactions.

payload_summary.fallback_suggested: FELLA R subprocess errored at runtime (currently 'argument is of length zero' on every sub6b-v3 task — W9 D4 stretch target); skip the network/diffusion paradigm and rely on ORA + mummichog
use run_ramp_enrichment (multi-DB ORA, broader namespace coverage) or run_metaboanalystr_psea (KEGG-specific ORA) instead

final_claims.claim_text: RaMP ORA identifies KEGG:map00380 Tryptophan metabolism as the top hit with an FDR of 1.46e-15 and a fold enrichment of 857.8, driven by six input metabolites.
MetaboAnalystR KEGG-ORA independently confirms the same pathway (hsa00380) with a p-value of 1.79e-07.
Mummichog m/z-direct analysis returns MUMM:tryptophan_metabolism with p=0.0021 and an overlap of 14 out of 15 network compounds.

react_result.final_narrative_text: Three independent enrichment paradigms converge on tryptophan metabolism as the dominant affected pathway in this differential metabolomics dataset. RaMP multi-DB ORA identifies KEGG:map00380 Tryptophan metabolism as the top hit with an FDR of 1.46e-15 and a fold enrichment of 857.8, driven by six input metabolites. MetaboAnalystR KEGG-ORA independently confirms the same pathway (hsa00380) with a p-value of 1.79e-07, and Mummichog m/z-direct analysis returns MUMM:tryptophan_metabolism with p=0.0021 and an overlap of 14 out of 15 network compounds. The six driver metabolites shared across RaMP and Mummichog hits are L-tryptophan, serotonin, melatonin, indoleacetaldehyde, tryptamine, and quinolinic acid. L-Tryptophan (KEGG:C00078) is the entry-point substrate; serotonin (KEGG:C00780) and melatonin (KEGG:C01598) represent the biogenic amine branch; indoleacetaldehyde (KEGG:C00637) and tryptamine (KEGG:C00398) are upstream intermediates; quinolinic acid (KEGG:C03722) belongs to the kynurenine branch of the same pathway. Pyrophosphate, iron, succinic acid, indole, and D-glucose are detected in the input set but do not appear in the tryptophan metabolism hit lists, suggesting they arise from unrelated processes. The convergence of an ORA result, a KEGG-ORA result, and an empirical m/z-network result on the same metabolic pathway provides strong cross-paradigm evidence that tryptophan metabolism is the primary biological signal.

{
  "narrative_text": "Three independent enrichment paradigms converge on tryptophan metabolism as the dominant affected pathway in this differential metabolomics dataset. RaMP multi-DB ORA identifies KEGG:map00380 Tryptophan metabolism as the top hit with an FDR of 1.46e-15 and a fold enrichment of 857.8, driven by six input metabolites. final_claims.claim_text: RaMP ORA identifies KEGG:map00380 Tryptophan metabolism as the top hit with an FDR of 1.46e-15 and a fold enrichment of 857.8, driven by six input metabolites.
MetaboAnalystR KEGG-ORA independently confirms the same pathway (hsa00380) with a p-value of 1.79e-07.
Mummichog m/z-direct analysis returns MUMM:tryptophan_metabolism with p=0.0021 and an overlap of 14 out of 15 network compounds.

final_react_result.final_narrative_text: Three independent enrichment paradigms converge on tryptophan metabolism as the dominant affected pathway in this differential metabolomics dataset. RaMP multi-DB ORA identifies KEGG:map00380 Tryptophan metabolism as the top hit with an FDR of 1.46e-15 and a fold enrichment of 857.8, driven by six input metabolites. MetaboAnalystR KEGG-ORA independently confirms the same pathway (hsa00380) with a p-value of 1.79e-07, and Mummichog m/z-direct analysis returns MUMM:tryptophan_metabolism with p=0.0021 and an overlap of 14 out of 15 network compounds. The six driver metabolites shared across RaMP and Mummichog hits are L-tryptophan, serotonin, melatonin, indoleacetaldehyde, tryptamine, and quinolinic acid. L-Tryptophan (KEGG:C00078) is the entry-point substrate; serotonin (KEGG:C00780) and melatonin (KEGG:C01598) represent the biogenic amine branch; indoleacetaldehyde (KEGG:C00637) and tryptamine (KEGG:C00398) are upstream intermediates; quinolinic acid (KEGG:C03722) belongs to the kynurenine branch of the same pathway. Pyrophosphate, iron, succinic acid, indole, and D-glucose are detected in the input set but do not appear in the tryptophan metabolism hit lists, suggesting they arise from unrelated processes. The convergence of an ORA result, a KEGG-ORA result, and an empirical m/z-network result on the same metabolic pathway provides strong cross-paradigm evidence that tryptophan metabolism is the primary biological signal.
